pairs.subject: multi-project
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/page.tsx:44 The plan page draws the composition list beside the plan, but a failed list read is passed on as an empty list. An unreadable list therefore looks the same as 'no compositions'. The sibling /projects page (page.tsx:28) throws in this case for exactly that reason.

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/page.tsx:44 Breaks level parity: a list that could not be read is shown as an empty list instead of as broken.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/_part/real.ts:99 Part writes are keyed by the minted projectId and the part id, never by a title.

pairs.subject: multi-project
pairs.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/_port/real.ts:135 The list (the wall) is served by the kernel's listProjects. For every listed project, up to LIST_LIMIT=100, it builds the full project model and view (parts, jobs, facts) and computes pips, ETA and USD at read time instead of reading a stored summary row. Wall cost therefore grows as N × depth.

techniques.evidence: packages/kernel/src/records/read.ts:305 Each list row is built from the full projectModel and view. This is the per-render fan-out the technique forbids; it is bounded at 100 but not pre-digested.

app/(studio)/projects/_port/real.ts:167 Rename changes only the title field and is addressed by id. The id is minted once at compose (real.ts:162: a slug of the first title plus a random suffix) and is never re-derived.
app/(studio)/projects/_port/real.ts:168 Discard goes through the kernel, which stamps discardedAt and emits project.discarded. The record and its events are kept: archival as a state, not a deletion.

pairs.subject: multi-project
pairs.evidence: lib/projects.ts:211 v1 browser projects get an opaque id minted at creation. Edits never touch it, the list reads summary rows only, and deletion counts what it will destroy before acting, so the identity, density and removal rules hold.

techniques.evidence: lib/projects.ts:211 The id is opaque and minted at admission. editProject cannot overwrite it (the comment at line 479). Archive import re-mints rows owned by another account (studioArchive.ts:67).
lib/projects.ts:279 The list reads only the project rows. Their progress rollup is kept by reportPhase, and the heavy step records are never loaded for the list.

lib/projects.ts:587 Removal counts what it will destroy before acting and refuses when the count cannot be read. v1 has no archived state, only delete, so this conforms to the 'removal enumerates' clause only.

pairs.registryProposal: project-onboarding-lifecycle does not say whether a manager with no archived state, whose only exit is a delete that enumerates and is confirmed, conforms or deviates; the technique should state it.

pairs.subject: multi-project
pairs.evidence: lib/import/project.ts:105 The import door derives the kernel project id from the foreign v1 id instead of minting a local key and storing a mapping. Duplicate detection (exists(id), line 197) only matches the same v1 id. A v1 project that was re-minted on its way through another account's archive import comes in as a second, unrelated twin.

techniques.evidence: lib/import/project.ts:105 The foreign id becomes the local identity, which the 'foreign identity is quarantined' rule forbids. Inside the plan, rename and the ledger link are correctly id-keyed (Plan.tsx:119).
app/(studio)/projects/_plan/Plan.tsx:157 After a discard the project's history is still reachable in the ledger by its id, so discard preserves rather than erases.
app/(studio)/projects/_plan/CompositionList.tsx:111 List rows are keyed by id, drill to the plan by id, and keep the current row highlighted beside the plan, so the drill holds its context.
